title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: custom engine agents for GCC users
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented block path and API are accurate. Hold the briefing because its indirect-only cost rating conflicts with documented hosting and service consumption costs, and it leaves GCC availability of the governance Graph API unresolved although Microsoft lists it as unavailable.

claims.claim: The roadmap says GCC-M users will be able to use custom engine agents.
claims.quote: Users in GCC-M will be able to use custom engine agents.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Custom engine agents let developers bring their own orchestration.
claims.quote: Unlike declarative agents, they give developers the flexibility to bring their own orchestration and AI services.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Build routes include Copilot Studio, Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, Teams SDK and Microsoft Foundry.
claims.quote: These agents can be created using Copilot Studio, the Microsoft 365 Agents SDK, Teams SDK or Microsoft Foundry, depending on your preferred development approach and hosting environment.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Pro-code custom engine development requires builder-provided orchestration and hosting.
claims.quote: For pro-code custom engine development, choose a supported SDK and provide your own orchestration and hosting.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio is a fully managed SaaS platform for the low-code route.
claims.quote: Because Copilot Studio is a fully managed SaaS platform that simplifies building custom engine agents, you can focus on crafting effective agent experiences without worrying about infrastructure, hosting, or governance.

claims.claim: Learn does not provide a GCC-specific custom engine agent feature page confirming this release.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom engine agents" "GCC" rollout availability; "custom engine agents" "GCC" "default". Read overview, prerequisites, known issues and Microsoft Copilot service description; results give general agents guidance, not a GCC-specific release page.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot service description lists declarative agents for GCC.
claims.quote: | Declarative agents | Yes | Yes | Yes⁸ | Not currently available |

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot service description lists Agent Builder for GCC.
claims.quote: | Agent Builder | Yes | Yes | Yes | Not currently available |

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions; changes
claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot service description feature table has no custom engine agents row.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom engine agents" "GCC" rollout availability. Read the complete Microsoft Copilot service description table: Agents & extensibility lists Declarative agents, Agent Builder, Microsoft 365 Copilot Connectors and Power Platform Connectors, not custom engine agents.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this GCC capability arrives on, off or requiring administrator enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom engine agents" "GCC" "default"; custom engine agents GCC default enabled rollout licensing meter availability. Read roadmap, overview, prerequisites, known issues and government guidance; no default for this GCC release was stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated how this GCC rollout is staged.
claims.quote: Searched: "custom engine agents" "GCC" rollout availability. Read roadmap, overview, prerequisites and service description; results include general GA history but no GCC staging schedule.

claims.claim: Third-party services integrated through connectors or Azure Bot Service skills are outside Copilot Studio US Government compliance and data protection commitments.
claims.quote: As a result, these third-party applications and services aren't covered by the Copilot Studio US Government compliance and data protection commitments.

claims.claim: Prompts to pro-code custom engine agents reach builder-controlled processing services.
claims.quote: This model allows you to use the Microsoft client and catalog infrastructure while keeping full control over orchestrator, language model, and API components. Components within your control enable prompt routing to multiple language models through multiple processing loops
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/custom-engine-agent-architecture to sources for the statement about prompts reaching builder-controlled processing.

claims.claim: Custom engine agent prompts and responses in Copilot Chat and Teams are stored under Microsoft 365 product terms.
claims.quote: Custom engine agent prompts and responses in Copilot Chat and Teams are stored in compliance with Microsoft 365 product terms and conditions and are managed as per the customer's instructions.

claims.claim: Administrators can use Content Search or Microsoft Purview to view and manage the stored prompts and responses.
claims.quote: To view and manage this stored data, admins can use Content Search or Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data are not currently available in GCC, GCCH or DoD.
claims.quote: Agents grounded in shared tenant work data aren't currently available in Microsoft 365 Government Community Cloud (GCC), Government Community Cloud High (GCCH), or Department of Defense (DoD) environments.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether the governance Graph API is available for GCC.
claims.quote:
| Feature Description | Product Surface | Core capability included with Microsoft cloud subscription | Premium capability | GCC Availability |
| Graph API provides access to agent registry, basic metadata and governance actions | Microsoft 365 admin center | No | Yes | No |
claims.fix: Replace 'it has no GCC column, so treat it as a reference until Microsoft confirms it for GCC' with 'the block reference has no GCC column, but the Microsoft Agent 365 service description lists the Graph API for agent registry and governance actions as unavailable in GCC.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-agent-365/microsoft-agent-365.

claims.claim: Cost is low, meaning indirect cost only, despite the rationale acknowledging builder hosting and licensing costs.
claims.quote:
cost: "low"
Low. Learn lists custom engine agents for Copilot Chat users and licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot users and says usage-based billing is not supported in GCC; builders still bear hosting and licensing costs that Learn does not price.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'variable' and replace its rationale with 'Variable. Pro-code custom engine agents incur hosting and Azure service consumption costs; no separate GCC-release licence or meter is published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/faq: 'You don't need a Microsoft 365 Copilot license to build custom engine agents by using Teams SDK. Instead, the cost depends on the Azure services consumed in the app.' The GCC restriction on Copilot usage billing does not remove external hosting costs.
